title: Q-Shield Layer B result
description: One live TLS handshake, observed on the wire. Layer A composes a handshake in-process and cannot produce any of the structural fields here. The key design property: structural facts are portable across machines while timings are not, so they are separated and the timing block carries its own publishable flag.

label.description: Which configuration this run exercised, e.g. pairwise or mismatch.

server_groups_accepted.description: Recorded so a deliberately-mismatched run is self-describing rather than looking like a failure.

outcome.description: A labelled result. Downgrade and rejection are outcomes, never errors: a silent downgrade inferred from the absence of a signal is exactly the reporting gap Layer B exists to close.

wire.description: Facts parsed from captured bytes. Never from a stack's own report string -- see layer-b-spec.md section 4.

unparsed_after_serverhello.description: Records after the ServerHello are encrypted. Counted, never claimed to be read.

structure.description: Properties of the protocol exchange. Portable across machines, so publishable from wherever the capture was taken.

ip_fragments.description: Counted, never silently reassembled -- whether a PQC handshake fragments is one of Layer B's own findings.

timing.description: A property of the machine, not the protocol. Never publishable unless the run states it happened on the measurement host.

publishable.description: False for any run on a laptop or a shared CI runner. A false value here means this figure must not reach a published surface.

name.description: Name for the code point, or its hex value when we cannot name it. Never guessed.

identity_verified.description: Whether this code point's identity is confirmed against a primary source. False means the name is #unverified, per CLAUDE.md's sourcing standard.
